tier_reason: First-party README tables. The imagecodecs table's harness (bench/bench_vs_imagecodecs.py) and per-run medians (bench/results/vs_imagecodecs/linux.json, mac.json, windows.json) are public and check identical decoded output, but no CPU model is named (only '20-core Apple silicon Mac', '64-core x86-64 Linux workstation', '4-core x86-64 Windows laptop') and the build flags behind the measured wheels are not stated, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README 'Codecs against imagecodecs' (opencodecs 0.5.0 vs imagecodecs 2026.8.16; Mac / Linux / Windows): TIFF-flavor LZW decode 3.33x / 3.07x / 2.94x and LZW encode 1.33x / 1.32x / 1.49x (own kernels, single-threaded on both sides); PackBits decode 3.32x / 2.81x / 1.52x; PNG RGB uint8 level 6 encode 3.45x / 3.68x / 1.12x, PNG decode 1.69x / 0.99x / 0.80x; JPEG quality 90 encode 2.68x / 3.91x / 0.97x, JPEG decode 1.56x / 1.80x / 1.01x; deflate level 6 encode 2.69x / 2.58x / 2.61x, decode 1.90x / 1.54x / 1.67x. Rows marked 'opencodecs threaded' (opencodecs on several threads by default, imagecodecs on one): JPEG 2000 lossless encode 8.05x / 4.66x / 2.73x and decode 7.64x / 4.57x / 2.71x; JPEG XL 2.30x to 10x (Mac lossless effort 3 encode 10x); BC7 decode 11x / 5.47x / 4.09x; BC1 decode 4.45x / 1.79x / 2.27x. Many rows are at 0.72x to 1.05x (zstd, lz4, brotli, blosc2, lzma, bz2, snappy, WebP, QOI, JPEG-LS, ZFP). README 'TIFF against tifffile' (4096x4096 uint16 tiled deflate+predictor): Linux 4.2x one reader at defaults, 1.4x forced single thread, 10.0x with 8 concurrent readers; Mac 3.3x / 1.1x / 3.9x; 3072x3072 uint8 144-tile deflate up to 13.2x (Linux, 8 readers); single-thread cells range 0.95x to 2.4x. Example absolute times (derived from page data, bench/results/vs_imagecodecs/linux.json medians): LZW decode 29.78 ms vs 91.52 ms; PNG encode 251.31 ms vs 924.51 ms; JPEG encode 20.93 ms vs 81.93 ms.
corrections.workload: Codec table: bench/bench_vs_imagecodecs.py, one codec operation per row at matched settings, opencodecs 0.5.0 against imagecodecs 2026.8.16. Each sample is a fresh Python process that imports one library and times one case (median of 5 to 40 calls after one warm-up); the driver alternates the two libraries in shuffled order for 5 rounds and the table cell is the ratio of round medians. Inputs are a synthetic 4096x4096 uint16 field (sin/cos plus Gaussian noise; 32 MB, 8 MB slice for lzma/bz2, 16 MB uint8 for LZW/PackBits) and 2048x2048 RGB uint8, uint16 and float32 views of it; BC1/BC7 decode random block bytes. Decode rows decode one imagecodecs-written bitstream and require identical output digests; lossless encode rows must round-trip. TIFF table: reads of tifffile-written files (4096x4096 uint16 tiled/striped, 3072x3072 uint8 with 144 tiles) against tifffile 2026.3.3 (Mac) and 2026.5.2 (Linux), median over fresh alternating processes, with both libraries at defaults, both forced to one thread, and 8 concurrent readers.
corrections.hardware: 20-core Apple silicon Mac (arm64, macOS), 64-core x86-64 Linux workstation whose cores sit in 16 four-core L3 groups, each measured process pinned to CPUs 8-11,72-75 (one group, 8 hardware threads, per linux.json metadata), and a 4-core x86-64 Windows laptop; exact CPU models not stated anywhere checked.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated with the tables beyond 'opencodecs 0.5.0 built as its CI wheels are' (TIFF table). README says vendored scientific compressors are source-built with -O3, LTO and hidden visibility; bench/README.md lists macOS 15.5 clang (Xcode) and Ubuntu gcc 13 for older regression baselines. imagecodecs 2026.8.16 from its own wheels. Python 3.12.13 (Linux), 3.12.9 (Mac), 3.12.6 (Windows) per result-file metadata. Harness: bench/bench_vs_imagecodecs.py.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 3 stars, 0 forks, 463 commits; published on PyPI (0.5.0 on 2026-10-02, 0.6.0 on 2026-10-03, 0.7.0 on 2026-10-04)
corrections.caveats: A Python package (Cython and C/C++ extensions bundling libspng, libdeflate, libjpeg-turbo, OpenJPEG, libjxl and others), not a new codec library. Where both packages wrap the same C library the speedups come from build and binding differences or default threading, not new algorithms: JPEG encode writes byte-identical-size output on both sides (2,437,855 bytes on all three hosts) and is 3.91x on Linux but 0.97x on Windows; JPEG 2000, JPEG XL, BC1 and BC7 rows compare opencodecs' default multi-threaded call (process CPU/wall 4 to 12) against imagecodecs' single-threaded default, so they are not per-core wins. PNG and deflate gains come from libdeflate versus zlib; opencodecs' PNG output is 6,493,730 bytes versus 6,437,751 for imagecodecs (about 0.9% larger, derived from page data). Its own kernels (TIFF LZW, PackBits) are the clean single-thread wins at about 3x. Many rows are at parity or slower (zstd, brotli, blosc2, lzma, ZFP encode 0.70x to 0.72x on Mac and Windows, PNG decode 0.80x on Windows, packed-integer decode 0.82x on Linux). The README says both packages use libjxl 0.12.0 while its capability matrix and install notes say vendored libjxl 0.11.2; on Linux lossy JPEG XL decodes differ by 1 in about a third of values and the lossy encode sizes differ (2,150,106 versus 2,238,951 bytes). The TIFF-versus-tifffile table has no matching harness or result file under bench/ (bench/bench_parallel_tiff.py uses a different in-process method). CPU models not named, so tier stays C. GitHub page shows latest release v0.5.0; 0.6.0 and 0.7.0 are on PyPI.

notes: Numbers in the record match the README. Strongest comparison: own TIFF LZW decode kernel at 2.94x to 3.33x single-threaded on all three hosts with identical output, then PNG encode on libspng+libdeflate (3.45x Mac, 3.68x Linux, 1.12x Windows) against imagecodecs (libpng+zlib); the large threaded rows compare different thread counts. Young single-author repo (3 stars) but very active and on PyPI.

tier_reason: Only a first-party README table (Tegra X1, Cortex-A57 at max 2.091 GHz, average of 1000 iterations). The repo ships no comparison harness: examples/render-*.cpp time a single NVJPG render with std::chrono and never call libjpeg-turbo, and no compiler, flags or libjpeg-turbo version are given for the table.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the table. The repo builds with meson (buildtype=release, gnu++20) on Linux or a devkitA64 Makefile (-O2 -march=armv8-a+crc+crypto+simd -mtune=cortex-a57) for Switch homebrew; libjpeg-turbo, stb_image, Pillow and nanoJPEG versions and build options are not stated.
corrections.hardware: Nvidia Tegra X1 SoC, Aarch64 Cortex-A57 at max 2.091 GHz, using the SoC's NVJPG hardware JPEG block for oss-nvjpg and the A57 CPU cores for libjpeg-turbo and the other software decoders. The Makefile targets Nintendo Switch homebrew (libnx, deko3d), so the board is likely a Switch, but the README does not say.
corrections.caveats: First-party README table only; the 1000-iteration averaging harness and the libjpeg-turbo, stb_image, Pillow and nanoJPEG runs are not in the repo. The shipped examples (examples/render-rgb.cpp, render-nx.cpp and others) time one decoder.render plus decoder.wait after the file is read and the JPEG headers are parsed, into an RGBA surface, so it is unknown whether the software timings cover the same steps. No compiler, flags or libjpeg-turbo version (or whether its NEON paths were enabled) are stated. Two test images only. This compares a fixed-function hardware decoder on the Tegra X1 against software decoders on its Cortex-A57 cores: the speedup (about 3.0x and 4.1x, derived from page data) comes from dedicated hardware, does not transfer to other SoCs, and frees the CPU rather than proving a faster algorithm. Baseline JPEGs only; progressive and arithmetic-coded files return an error. GPL-3.0.

notes: README numbers match the record exactly (NVJPG 2.036 / 15.997 ms vs libjpeg-turbo 6.127 / 66.341 ms). Last commit 2025-06-18 (about 15 months), so stale is right.

tier_reason: First-party single run. The harness is public (scripts/compare_load_speed.py: 1 warm-up pass, best of 3 timed passes, pixel-identity check on the first 10 pairs) and libpzp.so's gcc flags are in the Makefile, but no CPU model, OpenCV version or libpng build is stated, and the 500-image COCO set is not in the repo.

corrections.workload: scripts/compare_load_speed.py on 500 matched COCO val2017 panoptic segmentation label maps (3-channel uint8 RGB, varying resolutions): one untimed warm-up pass over both sets (fills the page cache), then 3 timed passes, best pass reported. PNG column: cv2.imread(IMREAD_UNCHANGED) plus a BGR-to-RGB numpy view; PZP column: PZP.read, a ctypes call into libpzp.so plus one memcpy into a numpy array, files encoded with USE_COMPRESSION, USE_RLE and USE_PALETTE (zstd). Pixel identity is checked on the first 10 pairs only.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc (version not stated); libpzp.so is built by the Makefile with -shared -fPIC -D_GNU_SOURCE -DINTEL_OPTIMIZATIONS -O3 -mavx2 -march=native -mtune=native, linked against system libzstd and liblz4 (versions not stated). OpenCV version and its PNG backend build not stated.
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers from one machine with no CPU model; the harness (scripts/compare_load_speed.py) is a Python loop comparing a ctypes call into libpzp.so against cv2.imread, so OpenCV's imread overhead sits in the PNG column. This compares two file formats (zstd with palette and RLE versus PNG's deflate), not a faster PNG decoder: the doc credits zstd decoding faster than zlib plus a flat layout. The dataset is segmentation label maps with few distinct colors, the README's own best case. libpzp.so is compiled with -DINTEL_OPTIMIZATIONS, but doc/performance.md says 3-channel images fall back to a scalar loop in the SSE2/AVX2 prefix-scan RLE decoder, so the SIMD path does not run on this dataset. Not compared with fpng, Wuffs, libspng or QOI. The output block in doc/performance.md is formatted slightly differently from what the current script prints, but the numbers agree (1141.2 / 500.6 ms = 2.28x). GPL-3.0.

notes: Numbers match doc/performance.md (1141.2 ms vs 500.6 ms best of 3, 2.28x; 4.1 MB vs 2.0 MB). Baseline is cv2.imread (OpenCV's PNG decoder, which the doc names as libpng). Weeks-old single-author repo (2 stars); kept on evidence, tier C.
